sanskrit_shloka:
कर्तुराज्ञया प्राप्यते फलम् |
कर्म किं परं कर्म तज्जडम् || १ ||
transliteration:
karturājñayā prāpyate phalam |
karma kiṁ paraṁ karma tajjaḍam || 1 ||
translation:
By the law/will of the Creator, the fruits of actions are realized.
How is action then supreme? It is not. It is inert.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text:
By the law/will of the Creator, the fruits of actions are realized.
How is action then supreme? It is not. It is inert.

translation:
The results of actions are impermanent and pass away.
Yet, their seeds form an ocean of Karma which becomes a barrier in the progress of a seeker.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text:
The results of actions are impermanent and pass away.
Yet, their seeds form an ocean of Karma which becomes a barrier in the progress of a seeker.

translation: Work which is performed as an offering to the Almighty, and done without any expectation of the fruits thereof, helps in purification of the mind and thereby leads one to Liberation or Realization.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Work which is performed as an offering to the Almighty, and done without any expectation of the fruits thereof, helps in purification of the mind and thereby leads one to Liberation or Realization.

translation: Among the actions performed by the body, voice and mind – puja (ritualistic worship),  japa (chanting) and contemplation (inner meditation) – each is superior to the other in an ascending order.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Among the actions performed by the body, voice and mind – puja (ritualistic worship),  japa (chanting) and contemplation (inner meditation) – each is superior to the other in an ascending order.

translation: Worshipping any of the eight forms, thinking they are all forms of God, is good worship (puja) of God.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Worshipping any of the eight forms, thinking they are all forms of God, is good worship (puja) of God.

translation: Singing the Lord’s praises is good, but better than that is loud chanting of japa, while superior to loud chanting is soft japa. However, best of all is silent, mental japa.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Singing the Lord’s praises is good, but better than that is loud chanting of japa, while superior to loud chanting is soft japa. However, best of all is silent, mental japa.

sanskrit_shloka:
आज्यधारया स्रोतसा समम् |
सरलचिन्तनं विरलतः परम् || ७ ||
transliteration:
ājyadhārayā srotasā samam |
saralacintanaṁ viralataḥ param || 7 ||
translation: Like an unbroken flow of oil, or a stream of water, continuous meditation is better than that which is interrupted.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Like an unbroken flow of oil, or a stream of water, continuous meditation is better than that which is interrupted.

translation:
Meditation without duality, that is meditating as ‘I am
HE’, is superior to meditation which assumes a separation between the Bhakta (devotee) and the beloved Lord.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text:
Meditation without duality, that is meditating as ‘I am
HE’, is superior to meditation which assumes a separation between the Bhakta (devotee) and the beloved Lord.

translation:
A state of void, free from thought, is gradually attained,
making abidance in the background state of ‘I AM’ complete. This is supreme devotion.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text:
A state of void, free from thought, is gradually attained,
making abidance in the background state of ‘I AM’ complete. This is supreme devotion.

sanskrit_shloka:
हृत्स्थले मनः स्वस्थता क्रिया |
भक्तियोगबोधाश्च निश्चितम् || १० ||
transliteration:
hṛtsthale manaḥ svasthatā kriyā |
bhaktiyogabodhāśca niścitam || 10 ||
translation: Fixing the mind in the Heart (Source) is true Karma (action), Bhakti (devotion), Yoga (action) and Jnana (knowledge).

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Fixing the mind in the Heart (Source) is true Karma (action), Bhakti (devotion), Yoga (action) and Jnana (knowledge).

translation: Through breath-control, the movement of the mind is contained, just as a bird is restrained when caught in a net.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Through breath-control, the movement of the mind is contained, just as a bird is restrained when caught in a net.

translation: The mind and pranas, which carry out various thought processes and actions within the body, emerge from one common source, the Supreme.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The mind and pranas, which carry out various thought processes and actions within the body, emerge from one common source, the Supreme.

sanskrit_shloka:
लयविनाशने उभयरोधने ।
लयगतं पुनर्भवति नो मृतम् ॥ १३॥
transliteration:
Layavināśane ubhayarodhane .
Layagataṃ punarbhavati no mṛtam .. 13..
translation: Mind control can be achieved through two modes – either through absorption/abeyance or through complete destruction. In the case of the first mode, the mind emerges again as it is merely absorbed in the void and hence temporarily held in abeyance. In contrast, through the second mode, when the mind is destroyed, it can never emerge again.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Mind control can be achieved through two modes – either through absorption/abeyance or through complete destruction. In the case of the first mode, the mind emerges again as it is merely absorbed in the void and hence temporarily held in abeyance. In contrast, through the second mode, when the mind is destroyed, it can never emerge again.

transliteration:
Prāṇa bandhanāllīna mānasam .
Eka cintanānnāśamet yadaḥ .. 14..
translation: When the mind is held in suspension through breath control, it must then be completely destroyed through one-pointed attention to that ONE reality.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: When the mind is held in suspension through breath control, it must then be completely destroyed through one-pointed attention to that ONE reality.

translation: What action remains for an exalted Yogi whose mind has been completely destroyed and who is ever established in the Self ?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: What action remains for an exalted Yogi whose mind has been completely destroyed and who is ever established in the Self ?

translation: When attention is withdrawn from objects and focused exclusively on the Self, Truth is revealed.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: When attention is withdrawn from objects and focused exclusively on the Self, Truth is revealed.

sanskrit_shloka:
मानसं तु किं मार्गणे कृते ।
नैव मानसं मार्ग आर्जवात् ॥ १७॥
transliteration:
Mānasaṃ tu kiṃ mārgaṇe kṛte .
Naiva mānasaṃ mārga ārjavāt .. 17..
translation: When one inquires: “What is the mind?”, he finds out that there is no mind. This is the direct path to Reality.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: When one inquires: “What is the mind?”, he finds out that there is no mind. This is the direct path to Reality.

sanskrit_shloka:
वृत्तयस्त्वहं वृत्तिमाश्रिताः ।
वृत्तयो मनो विद्ध्यहं मनः ॥ १८॥
transliteration:
Vṛttayastvahaṃ vṛttimāśritāḥ .
Vṛttayo mano viddhyahaṃ manaḥ .. 18..
translation: Mind is nothing but a bundle of thoughts. These thoughts depend upon the I-thought alone. Hence the mind is nothing but this I-thought.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Mind is nothing but a bundle of thoughts. These thoughts depend upon the I-thought alone. Hence the mind is nothing but this I-thought.

sanskrit_shloka:
अहमयं कुतो भवति चिन्वतः ।
अयि पतत्यहं निजविचारणम् ॥ १९॥
transliteration:
Ahamayaṃ kuto bhavati cinvataḥ .
Ayi patatyahaṃ nijavicāraṇam .. 19..
translation: Ask the question: “From where does this I-thought arise?” On inquiring deeply, the I-thought will vanish. This is Self-Inquiry.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Ask the question: “From where does this I-thought arise?” On inquiring deeply, the I-thought will vanish. This is Self-Inquiry.

transliteration:
Ahami nāśa bhājyaham ahaṃtayā .
Sphurati hṛtsvayaṃ paramapūrṇasat .. 20..
translation: When the I-thought or Ego is destroyed, the real I springs forth on its own in the spiritual Heart and shines as ‘I-I’, in all its fulness.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: When the I-thought or Ego is destroyed, the real I springs forth on its own in the spiritual Heart and shines as ‘I-I’, in all its fulness.

translation: And this unbroken continuous ‘I-I’ is the real I, as the I-thought (egoic I) disappears and dissolves in deep sleep.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: And this unbroken continuous ‘I-I’ is the real I, as the I-thought (egoic I) disappears and dissolves in deep sleep.

translation: This real ‘I-I’ is the only Truth or Reality. Neither the body, nor the senses, nor the vital air (prana), nor breath, nor intellect, nor ignorance may be considered real as they are all gross, inert, insentient and illusory.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: This real ‘I-I’ is the only Truth or Reality. Neither the body, nor the senses, nor the vital air (prana), nor breath, nor intellect, nor ignorance may be considered real as they are all gross, inert, insentient and illusory.

sanskrit_shloka:
सत्त्वभासिका चित्क्ववेतरा ।
सत्तया हि चिच्चित्तया ह्यहम् ॥ २३॥
transliteration:
Sattvabhāsikā citkvavetarā .
Sattayā hi ciccittayā hyaham .. 23..
translation: Is there any other thing apart from Consciousness that illumines existence? Indeed, existence itself is Consciousness and Consciousness is ‘I AM’.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Is there any other thing apart from Consciousness that illumines existence? Indeed, existence itself is Consciousness and Consciousness is ‘I AM’.

translation: Between the jiva (the individual) and Ishwara (Unity), there is a difference only with respect to the equipment (gross and subtle bodies) but from the standpoint of True Nature, the Absolute Reality alone is.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Between the jiva (the individual) and Ishwara (Unity), there is a difference only with respect to the equipment (gross and subtle bodies) but from the standpoint of True Nature, the Absolute Reality alone is.

translation: When the various conditionings of body-mind and identifications with name and form are shed, the Self is realized. The vision of the Lord as Self is true SelfRealization.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: When the various conditionings of body-mind and identifications with name and form are shed, the Self is realized. The vision of the Lord as Self is true SelfRealization.

translation: Since the Self is non-dual, establishing oneself in the Self alone is the vision of the Self, and that alone is abidance in the Self.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Since the Self is non-dual, establishing oneself in the Self alone is the vision of the Self, and that alone is abidance in the Self.

translation: Consciousness transcends all dualities and is devoid of the thought of knowledge, as well as the thought of ignorance. Is there any knowledge other than Self Awareness itself, to know the Self ?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Consciousness transcends all dualities and is devoid of the thought of knowledge, as well as the thought of ignorance. Is there any knowledge other than Self Awareness itself, to know the Self ?

translation: What is the nature of ‘Me’ – the Self? Thus inquiring one realizes the Self as Indestructible, Unborn, Perfect and of the nature of Consciousness and bliss.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: What is the nature of ‘Me’ – the Self? Thus inquiring one realizes the Self as Indestructible, Unborn, Perfect and of the nature of Consciousness and bliss.

sanskrit_shloka:
बन्धमुक्त्यतीतं परं सुखम् ।
विन्दतीह जीवस्तु दैविकः ॥ २९॥
transliteration:
Bandha muktyatītaṃ paraṃ sukham .
Vindatīha jīvastu daivikaḥ .. 29..
translation: The individual who has realized the Divine State (his own real nature) gains supreme happiness and bliss, beyond bondage and freedom, here, in this very world.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The individual who has realized the Divine State (his own real nature) gains supreme happiness and bliss, beyond bondage and freedom, here, in this very world.

translation: Self-Inquiry, devoid of ego, is a great penance. Realize this truth articulated by Sri Ramana.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Self-Inquiry, devoid of ego, is a great penance. Realize this truth articulated by Sri Ramana.
